classification.difficultyReason: Extract the specified triangles from larger figures, recognise common sides and infer an unmarked vertically opposite angle pair before selecting a congruence test.

content.prompt: Determine a test that could be used to prove these triangles are congruent.

spec.description: Slanted quadrilateral with one-tick sides AB and DC, two-tick sides BC and AD, and dashed diagonal AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens; no answer is drawn.

answer.worked: $AD=BC$, $DC=AB$ and $AC$ is common. The triangles are congruent by SSS.

spec.description: Parallelogram-shaped perimeter AB–BD–DC–CA with matching parallel marks, shared dashed BC and two marked angle pairs.
spec.mathematics: Angle ABC=BCD=a°, angle ACB=CBD=b°, BC is common.
spec.answerVisibility: Marked angles and parallel arrows are permanent givens.

answer.worked: $\angle ABC=\angle BCD=a^\circ$ and $\angle ACB=\angle CBD=b^\circ$. Also, $BC$ is common. The triangles are congruent by AAS.

spec.description: Four equally marked perimeter sides; diagonals CA and DB intersect at E with a right-angle square in AEB.
spec.mathematics: AB=AD, EA is common and the angles BEA and DEA are right angles.
spec.answerVisibility: No congruence result is printed in the diagram.

answer.worked: $\angle BEA=\angle DEA=90^\circ$. The hypotenuses satisfy $BA=DA$, and $EA$ is common. The triangles are congruent by RHS.

spec.description: Tilted rectangle with parallel-arrow pairs, right-angle squares at A and C, dashed DB and equal marked angles ABD and BDC.
spec.mathematics: Angle BAD=BCD=90°, angle ABD=BDC=a°, BD is common.

answer.worked: $\angle BAD=\angle BCD=90^\circ$ and $\angle ABD=\angle BDC=a^\circ$. Also, $BD$ is common. The triangles are congruent by AAS.

spec.description: Tilted rectangle with all four right-angle squares, AB=DC, AD=BC and intersecting dashed diagonals AC and DB.
spec.mathematics: AB=DC, BC is common and angle ABC=DCB=90° give SAS directly.
spec.answerVisibility: The source answer is excluded from the question diagram.

answer.worked: $AB=DC$, $BC$ is common and $\angle ABC=\angle DCB=90^\circ$. These are the included angles, so the triangles are congruent by SAS.

spec.description: Slanted quadrilateral with AB double-ticked, AD and BC single-ticked, intersecting diagonals and four angle sectors labelled a° or b°.
spec.mathematics: AD=BC, angle ADE=EBC=a°, angle DAE=BCE=b°, and vertically opposite angles AED=BEC.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens, including the redundant AB tick, remain visible.

answer.worked: $\angle ADE=\angle EBC=a^\circ$ and $\angle AED=\angle BEC$ because they are vertically opposite. Also, $AD=BC$. The triangles are congruent by AAS.

spec.description: Square-shaped perimeter with four equal sides and four right-angle squares; both diagonals and all four equally double-ticked half-diagonals are blue.
spec.mathematics: AB=AD=DC=CB and AE=BE=CE=DE. Each named triangle has two double-ticked sides and one single-ticked side.
spec.answerVisibility: Equal-side marks are source givens; no response is embedded.

answer.worked: $AB=AD=DC=CB$ and $AE=BE=CE=DE$. Each triangle has two equal diagonal segments and one equal perimeter side. All four triangles are congruent by SSS.

spec.description: Slanted quadrilateral with opposite equal-side pairs, intersecting dashed diagonals, and equal angles CDE and ABE. No parallel or right-angle marks are added.
spec.mathematics: AB=DC, angle ABE=CDE=a°, angle AEB=DEC by vertically opposite angles.
spec.answerVisibility: No inferred markings or supplied answer are drawn.

answer.worked: $\angle ABE=\angle CDE=a^\circ$ and $\angle AEB=\angle DEC$ because they are vertically opposite. Also, $AB=DC$. The triangles are congruent by AAS.
